subject: Mutual Roadmap & measurable acceptance signals — ClearWave pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@clearwave.com>, Elena Torres <elena.t@clearwave.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft mutual roadmap + first-pass measurable signals (pilot)

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Attached is a first-pass MAP and the sample eval test set (zip). We put the document together around concrete signals we think will demonstrate the pilot has met your objectives and ours. High level:

- Goal: Validate integrated inference for claims triage at 50 concurrent workflows, with production-like latency and a human-review concordance target.
- Window: 4-week evaluation (staged: smoke -> ramp -> production canary).
- Decision owner (ClearWave): Elena Torres (product) — please confirm.

Key measurable signals (first-pass):
- Latency: P90 end-to-end inference <= 350 ms for 95% of requests during ramp; canary target P90 <= 300 ms.
- Error rate: API error rate (5xx or model failures) < 1% sustained.
- Quality: Human-label concordance >= 92% on the 1,000-sample holdout; per-class recall >= 88% for top 3 priority labels.
- Throughput: Sustained 50 concurrent sessions with cold-start spike test (simulate 200 req/s for 10s) without degradation beyond latency SLO.
- Safety/false positives: FP rate <= 5% on flagged categories (we can compute on your annotated set).

Exit / holdback criteria we recommend (examples):
- Block: Missing SOC2 evidence or inability to sign data residency addendum.
- Hold: Latency/P95 > 700 ms during ramp for more than one sustained hour (escalate).
- Rollback trigger: More than 3 production-like regressions in quality over a rolling 48h window.

Acceptance tests (what we'll run):
1) Smoke: end-to-end flow with 50 golden records — verification within 2 business days.
2) Concordance: blind sampling of 1,000 records — compute agreement metrics vs your reviewers.
3) Load: 4x planned concurrency stress for 30m to validate autoscale and batching behavior.
4) Compliance checklist: KMS integration check, audit log sample, and retention confirmation.

Deliverables from Redwood during evaluation:
- MAP spreadsheet with owners & dates (attached).
- Test harness + scripts to run the smoke + load tests.
- Weekly scorecard (latency, errors, quality).

Questions for you: who will own sign-off on each of the bullets above (latency, quality, compliance)? Also can you confirm preferred cutover week (we suggested Sep 14 — Sep 18)?

Attaching: ClearWave_MAP_v1.xlsx, eval_testset_v0.2.zip (attachments).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short alignment call.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Elena Torres <elena.t@clearwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@clearwave.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft mutual roadmap + first-pass measurable signals (pilot)

Thanks Ben — useful start. A few clarifying notes inline: 

> Key measurable signals (first-pass):
> - Latency: P90 end-to-end inference <= 350 ms for 95% of requests during ramp; canary target P90 <= 300 ms.

Can you separate network + model compute latency vs "end-to-end"? Our baseline includes a downstream enrichment call that adds ~80ms — we need model-only and end-to-end figures so we can decide where to optimize.

> - Quality: Human-label concordance >= 92% on the 1,000-sample holdout; per-class recall >= 88% for top 3 priority labels.

The 1,000 sample set is fine, but we need per-segment thresholds. For example: auto-approved claims vs manual triage must have different tolerances. Also — what confidence threshold are you using to compute concordance?

> Exit / holdback criteria we recommend (examples):
> - Block: Missing SOC2 evidence or inability to sign data residency addendum.

This is non-negotiable. We will not proceed without KMS/HSM integration evidence. Can you confirm that Redwood will provide an extractable audit log sample?

A couple of asks:
- Please provide the mapping of which Redwood owners will be responsible for each acceptance item (e.g., who runs the load test, who owns the weekly scorecard).
- We want explicit rollback conditions for false positives in the "safety" categories: suggest a numeric threshold and an action (pause + human review).

If you can address the above and separate latency into model vs network, we can confirm sign-off owners and commit to the Sep 14 target week.

—Elena
Elena Torres
Product Lead, ClearWave Health
elena.t@clearwave.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.t@clearwave.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@clearwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft mutual roadmap + first-pass measurable signals (pilot)

Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the quick feedback, Elena. To make this operational we propose the following concrete additions to the MAP (I attached a short rubric PDF):

1) Split latency reporting into two metrics in the scorecard: 
   - Model_compute_p90 (server-side only, excludes ClearWave network/enrichment) — acceptance threshold: <= 240 ms for ramp; canary <= 210 ms.
   - End_to_end_p90 — acceptance threshold: <= 350 ms for ramp; explains your 80ms enrichment component so we can analyze optimization scope.

2) Quality definitions and confidence: we will use a calibrated confidence threshold (>= 0.65) to surface auto-approvals. Concordance will be computed at that threshold and on an unthresholded classification basis for error analysis. We'll produce per-segment thresholds (auto vs manual triage).

3) Safety/rollback numeric rule: if flagged-category false positive rate exceeds 5% in a 24h window AND the customer review pass-rate for those cases drops by >6 percentage points vs baseline, we pause auto-approval and kick the incident playbook (notify product + CS + infra).

4) Ownership matrix (quick):
   - Redwood: run load tests, provide model_compute metrics, host test harness scripts, deliver weekly scorecard (Ben/Marissa).
   - ClearWave: provide annotated holdout, own final sign-off on quality thresholds, run downstream enrichment latency tests in your environment.

5) Timeline:
   - Week 0 (prep): 8/24 — exchange keys, finalize test set, KMS audit extract scheduled.
   - Week 1 (smoke): 9/7 — smoke verification on golden set.
   - Week 2 (ramp): 9/14 — ramp with incremental traffic to 50 concurrent.
   - Week 3 (stress & concordance): 9/21 — run load + 1,000-sample concordance.
   - Week 4 (canary decision): 9/28 — post-test decision meeting.

Please confirm the owners we listed (I assigned Ben / Marissa to the Redwood tasks). Ben — please attach the scorecard template and the updated MAP with owners in the column as discussed.

I attached acceptance_rubric_v1.pdf for your review. Once Elena confirms owners and the KMS/audit commitment, we will lock the cutover week and circulate the DocuSign for the evaluation addendum.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
+1 (650) 555-0127

Thanks Hannah — this looks actionable. A couple quick procurement items before we lock dates: 

- We need the evaluation addendum to include a 30-day limited liability clause that reflects pilot scope (we will provide redline suggestions).
- Please confirm who at Redwood will provide the KMS audit extract; we need an exported sample event set to validate logging.

If you can have the MAP updated with ownership and the addendum link I can route it to procurement and legal for a fast review. Also the DocuSign link would be helpful once the addendum is attached.

Samir
